      Active Dutch

      Language schoolNetherlands: Alphen aan den Rijn6–15 h a month

      Dutch for expats in Alphen aan den Rijn and online: a beginners' group course, private lessons, the Keep Talking Dutch conversation club, plus a free trial lesson and a free 5-day speaking challenge.

      CA

      CVO adult education centres

      Language schoolBelgium: Antwerpen, Gent, Brussel, Leuven16–48 h a month

      Flemish government-funded adult education centres (Centra voor Volwassenenonderwijs) offer full NT2 courses at subsidised prices. Your Huis van het Nederlands or Atlas can refer you.

      €1.50 per lesson hour at the first level (max €180 in total), €0.60 per hour at higher levels, €0.30 with some reductions. Free with an inburgering contract or certificate. Books are extra.

      IV

      Inburgering via your gemeente

      GovernmentNetherlands: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Den Haag, Utrecht +340–80 h a month

      If you are required to complete civic integration (Wet inburgering 2021), your city hall arranges and pays for your learning route to B1. Volunteers who aren't required can sometimes join, or borrow from DUO.

      Free if your gemeente is responsible for your integration; otherwise a DUO loan is possible.

      KS

      Kickstart School

      Language schoolNetherlands: Den Haag12–40 h a month

      A language school in The Hague with group courses from beginner to advanced, in the classroom (max. 10), online (max. 8) or hybrid. Once a week or semi-intensive twice a week. Also a free Kickstart School toolkit with vocabulary, grammar tips, worksheets and links to practise.

      Free toolkit. Once-a-week group course €420 for 24 hours (€450 from 1 January 2027), book extra (about €48.50). A0–A2 in two courses €840. Basic Dutch for au pairs €380. Students and au pairs get €40 off some courses. Semi-intensive courses (48 hours) are listed at €720, but that page shows old dates, so check with the school.

    Hi, I'm Inka

    I moved to the Netherlands in 2019 and have been learning Dutch on and off ever since. On Instagram at @dutchlearning, I'm picking up Dutch again, and I hope to help more learners like me reach their goals.

    A lot of readers ask me: where should I start, and what's worth paying for? The thing is, the same resource doesn't suit everyone. That's why I made this website. It collects free and paid options and lets you filter them by your own budget, level and schedule.

    All listed resources were discovered by myself or other contributors. Each resource must have enough information for me to verify. No ads are involved. I hope to collect as many good-quality resources as possible through crowd power.
